Gurbir Singh, J.
1.
Dissatisfied with the amount of award dated 01.08.2018, the appellants-claimants have filed the present appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation.
The claim petition was filed on account of death of Jaggu Lal in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 31.07.2017.
The deceased was husband of appellant No.1 and father of appellant No.2.

The claimants were awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,45,200/-.
2.
The present appeal is accompanied with an application i.e. CM No.9-CII of 2023 seeking condonation of delay of 774 days in its filing.
The reason stated for the delay is that appellant No.1 did not know about the limitation period.
At the relevant time, there were corona pandemic restrictions.

After the death of her husband, since appellant No.1 was not having any source of income, so, she along with her minor 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:011015 son went to her parents' house at West Bengal.
She came to her house at Jalandhar in 2022.
3. I have heard the submission of learned counsel for the appellants and have gone through the file.
4. The delay is inordinate.

The law of limitation is found upon maxims such as "Interest Reipublicae Ut Sit Finis Litium" which means that litigation must come to an end in the interest of society as a Momena Bibi And Another vs Raj Kumar @ Raju And Another on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179046423/
1 whole, and "vigilantibus non dormientibus Jura subveniunt" which means that the law assists those that are vigilant with their rights, and not those that sleep thereupon.

entities.text: Momena Bibi And Another vs Raj Kumar @ Raju And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The Limitation Act, 1963 provides for period of limitation for any suit, appeal or application and these are liable to be dismissed if filed beyond the prescribed period.
The applicant has to satisfy the court with sufficient cause.
Law of limitation is substantive.
Condonation of delay is an exception.
Only on genuine reasons, delay can be condoned by exercising the power of discretion.
6. In the instant case, the award was passed in the year 2018 and the present appeal was filed after a delay of 774 days i.e. more than 2 years.
One cannot sleep over the matter for such a long period and suddenly woke up and approach the Court whenever finds fit.
One must be vigilant enough for his rights.
A mere bald statement that she was not advised by her counsel at Jalandhar and does not understand the local 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:011015 dialect is not of any help to her.
Another ground taken that during the relevant period, there was covid pandemic, is also not of any help to her, as the award was passed in August, 2018 and the Corona pandemic started in March, 2020.
There was sufficient period for her to approach the court for an appeal before the Corona pendamic restrictions started, but she remained silent upto 2022.
7. In case Majji Sannemma @ Sanyasirao Versus Reddy Sridevi and others-2021(18) SCC 384, the Regular Second Appeal was filed along with an application for condonation of delay.

entities.text: Majji Sannemma @ Sanyasirao Versus Reddy Sridevi and others-2021(18) SCC 384
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court condoned the delay in filing the appeal, however, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there was no sufficient explanation for condonation of delay.
In the said judgment, various judgments were discussed, however, the delay was not condoned.

8. In the case of Basawaraj and another Versus Special Land Acquisition Officer, (2013) 14 SCC 81, it is held by Hon'ble Apex Court that the discretion to condone the delay has to be exercised judiciously based on facts and circumstances of each case.

entities.text: Basawaraj and another Versus Special Land Acquisition Officer, (2013) 14 SCC 81
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The expression "sufficient cause" cannot be liberally interpreted if negligence, inaction or lack of bona fides is attributed to the party.
Even though limitation may harshly affect rights of a party but it has to be applied with all its rigour when prescribed by statute.

In case a party has acted with negligence, lack of bona fides or there is inaction, then there cannot be any justified ground for condoning the delay even by imposing 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:011015 conditions.
Each application for condonation of delay has to be decided within the framework laid down by this Court.
If courts start condoning delay where no sufficient cause is made out by imposing conditions then that would amount to violation of statutory principles and showing utter disregard to legislature.
9. In case Lingeswaran and others Versus Thirunagalingam, 2022(2) R.C.R. (Civil) 319, it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that Court has no power to extend period of limitation on equitable grounds.

entities.text: Lingeswaran and others Versus Thirunagalingam, 2022(2) R.C.R. (Civil) 319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. There is no sufficient explanation for condoning the delay of 774 days in filing the appeal.
The court cannot entertain any appeal at such a belated stage on the ground of equity.
Accordingly, this Court finds that the reasons mentioned by the applicant-appellant for condoning the delay of 774 days in filing the appeal are not sufficient.
